name: Blythe Ferry
significance: Tennessee River crossing used by 9 overland detachments carrying approximately 9,839 people

name: Mantle Rock
significance: Natural sandstone arch (188 ft long, ~30 ft high) where detachments sheltered while waiting to cross the Ohio River. The Hildebrand detachment camped here for approximately two weeks.

name: Berry's Ferry / Golconda
significance: Ohio River crossing point into southern Illinois

name: Trail of Tears State Park
significance: Mississippi River crossing site. Now a Missouri state park commemorating the removal.

name: Waterloo Landing
significance: Water route transfer point on the Tennessee River

name: Hopkinsville
significance: Burial site of White Path and Fly Smith, Cherokee leaders who died during the march

name: Mrs. Webber's Place
significance: Primary arrival and disbandment site in Indian Territory for overland detachments

name: Tahlequah
significance: New Cherokee capital established 1839; remains the Cherokee Nation headquarters today

name: Fort Coffee
significance: Water route terminus in Indian Territory
